Rules:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.

ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.

ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.

ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.

ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.

ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

plans.note: Primary review at Section 21; check mutuality of the cap, the multiplier of Fees, exclusion of indirect damages, and the scope of "Excluded Claims" as defined in Section 1. Confirm data breach, confidentiality and IP indemnity sit outside the cap.

Section 20 should contain Vendor IP infringement plus negligence/wilful misconduct and data breach indemnities; verify any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data rights only) and that Section 21 does not cap Excluded Claims. Cross-check Sections 14 and 15 for IP/data hooks.

No dedicated restrictive covenant section in the outline; scan Sections 2 (scope), 12 (Customer responsibilities), 13 (access/licence restrictions) and 30 (General) for disguised limits on competing products or in-house builds before concluding absent.

Look for sole-source or "all requirements" language in Sections 2 and 4 (Order Forms and Affiliate Orders) and in Sections 12 and 7; any exclusivity should be deleted or narrowed to the specific ordered scope.

Direction check: an MFN favouring us is acceptable, but any obligation for us to offer Vendor best terms must go. Most likely to appear in pricing (Section 7) or ordering (Section 4); otherwise absent.

No standalone non-solicit heading; check Section 30 (General) and Sections 12 and 16 for hiring restrictions. If present, seek mutuality, 12-month cap and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 is the main termination clause; confirm Customer convenience termination on ~30 days' notice without penalty or early-termination fee (check Sections 7 and 10 for wind-down charges) and that Vendor has no mid-term convenience right.
Section 8 governs term and renewal; test the non-renewal notice window (target 30 days, not 90) and any uplift cap on renewal Fees, cross-checking the pricing mechanics in Section 7.

Section 28 sets governing law, venue and any arbitration; confirm an approved jurisdiction (NY, DE, CA or England and Wales) and courts rather than offshore arbitration. Check Section 29 only if venue/service of process is cross-referenced.

Section 24 covers assignment and change of control; secure our right to assign to Affiliates and successors without consent and delete any Vendor termination or repricing right triggered by our change of control. Section 30 may hold a residual assignment clause.

Direction check in Section 14 (Deliverables ownership) and Section 15 (Customer Data): we must own paid-for Deliverables and all Customer Data, with no assignment or broad licence-back to Vendor. Review the Section 1 definitions of Deliverable, Customer Data and Vendor Technology, and any feedback/licence language in Section 13.

Section 13 is the licence grant; extend scope to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and remove any "revocable at will" or unilateral suspension language. Cross-check Affiliate ordering in Section 4.

Section 22 likely contains Vendor audits of our usage: limit to once per 12 months, 10+ business days' notice, business hours, remote/off-site where feasible, at Vendor's cost absent material underpayment. Section 23 records obligations may support or duplicate this.
Direction check: service credits in Section 3 favour us and stay, but strike liquidated damages, penalties or interest-style charges payable by us in Sections 7, 9 and 21.

Section 19 is the warranty clause; seek a professional-services and Deliverable conformity warranty of at least 90 days with re-performance plus refund as remedy, and resist "sole remedy" narrowing. Cross-check performance standards in Section 3 and acceptance in Section 6.

Section 18 exists; confirm coverage lines and limits (CGL, professional/E&O, cyber, workers' comp), certificate and notice-of-cancellation obligations, given Vendor handles Customer Data under Sections 15 and 17.

Check Sections 7 and 4 for committed spend, minimum volumes or take-or-pay true-ups and any non-reduction of quantities at renewal in Section 8; if present, pair with a convenience exit or reduction right.

Section 11 addresses transition assistance and data return; verify a minimum assistance period at then-current rates, export in a usable format, and deletion/certification, reconciled with the post-termination effects in Section 10 and data rights in Section 15.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

paragraphs.text: 20. INDEMNIFICATION

20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

20.3 Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.

20.4 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.

20.5 For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

paragraphs.text: 21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

payload.snippet: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.

Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

paragraphs.text: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

paragraphs.text: 12. CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

Kind: presence

No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.

Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.

Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

paragraphs.text: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

2.2 Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

2.3 Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.

No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.

Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN obligation on us (Customer), not on Vendor: we would have to extend Silverline the best terms we give any other technology supplier. It is unqualified as to product, duration, and comparability, which is the playbook walk-away position (open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better terms given to a third party). The preferred position is no MFN burdening Customer, so we delete the clause; MFN pricing in our favour would remain welcome. Deletion also resolves the duplicate "7.2" numbering with the invoicing clause at p0028.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the open-ended obligation for us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, as we do not accept MFN obligations running against the Customer. An MFN in our favour remains welcome; if Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

content.text: Section 20 is complete and Section 21.3 expressly excludes indemnification obligations from the liability cap. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets and exceeds the preferred position. 20.1 gives a Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, with no customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs. 20.2 adds the remaining preferred triggers: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (plus bodily injury/property damage). 20.4 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no adverse settlement without consent). 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate and refund) expressly "in addition to" the defence obligation, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. The Customer-side indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Direction is correct: the substantive burden falls on Vendor. Liability treatment also favours us: Section 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include a Party's indemnification obligations, IP infringement, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the 21.1 cap entirely — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Section 19.4 and 19.5 further confirm no warranty remedy or disclaimer limits the indemnities. No redline required.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

content.text: Section 21 matches the preferred position closely. No hidden caps in warranty/indemnity sections, and "Fees" is a substantive recurring-revenue base.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. (1) Cap: § 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual") and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 — the exact basis and floor we require, using the preferred "paid or payable" formulation rather than "paid". (2) Cap base is not illusory: "Fees" (§ 1.5, p0007) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other Order Form amounts, i.e. substantive recurring revenue; the carve-out of a one-time implementation charge does not undermine the base, and the USD 1,000,000 floor protects against a low-fee first year. (3) Indirect damages: § 21.2 excludes consequential/indirect damages mutually ("neither Party"), and helpfully deems data-restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs to be direct damages — better than our position. (4) Carve-outs: "Excluded Claims" (§ 21.3) sits outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion and covers every required item — breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement/misappropriation of the other Party's IP. So the § 20.1 IP indemnity, § 20.2 data-breach indemnity, and §§ 15–17 data/confidentiality/security obligations are all uncapped. (5) § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and is not limited by the section, as we require. Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: Clause 12.4 imposes a one-way restrictive covenant on Customer only: 18 months post-termination, covering any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term (not just personnel involved in the Services), and barring "engage" as well as "solicit" (effectively a no-hire). There is no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out and no mutuality, so it fails the playbook fallback on duration, scope, no-hire and carve-outs. It also conflicts with clause 12.3, which records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire persons responding to general recruitment. Preferred position is no non-solicit on Customer, so we delete 12.4; the fallback (mutual, 12 months, involved personnel, standard carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Clause 2.2, ¶p0013**

Clause 2.2 provides that "Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" — an unlimited exclusive-dealing obligation on us for the full term, with no product-category limit, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit. That is the playbook walk-away position, and it directly contradicts clause 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment; declining to sign another Order Form is not a breach).

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** delete ¶p0013 in full. No exclusivity running in our favour is affected, and the licence grant in § 13 remains expressly non-exclusive.

**Comment delivered:** "[Playbook] We deleted the sole-and-exclusive provider commitment in clause 2.2 because our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on us, and the clause conflicts with clause 2.1 (no minimum or purchase commitment). If Silverline needs volume assurance, we can discuss a non-exclusive statement or exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months that ends automatically on any service-level or delivery failure."

**Finding: Deviation (medium) — Section 7.2, paragraph p0027**

The agreement contains one MFN clause, and it runs the wrong way. Section 7.2 requires that *"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier."* This binds us, not Silverline, and it is completely open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no comparability carve-outs. That matches the playbook's walk-away description of an unqualified obligation to extend the Vendor any better terms given to a third party.

**Action taken:** Deleted p0027 in full (validated, `ok:true`). No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is affected. As a side benefit, the deletion clears the duplicate "7.2" numbering shared with the invoicing clause at p0028.

**Redline comment:** "[Playbook] We deleted the open-ended obligation for us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, as we do not accept MFN obligations running against the Customer. An MFN in our favour remains welcome; if Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs."

Aligned with precedent `seed-mfn` (Cedar Marketplace Agreement, May 2025). Fallback offered in the comment if Silverline pushes back.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 20 of the MSA already delivers the full preferred position on Vendor indemnification:

- **IP indemnity (20.1):** Vendor defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer *and its Affiliates* (plus directors, officers, employees, agents) against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP — and notably without the usual customer-modification / combination / specification exclusions we would have accepted as fallback.
- **Misconduct triggers (20.2):** Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury/death/property damage; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
- **Procedure (20.4):** Prompt notice qualified by a material-prejudice standard, cooperation at the *indemnifying* Party's expense, control of defence, and no settlement admitting fault or imposing non-monetary obligations without our consent.
- **Remedies (20.5):** Procure / modify / replace / terminate-and-refund, expressly *in addition to* the defence obligation, with Vendor barred from terminating unaffected Services.
- **Customer's indemnity (20.3) is properly narrow:** limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or Vendor instructions.

I also confirmed the indemnity is not undercut elsewhere. Section 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include each Party's indemnification obligations, IP infringement, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud — so Vendor's indemnity sits entirely **outside** the 21.1 liability cap, which is stronger than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap. Sections 19.4 and 19.5 add that no warranty remedy or implied-warranty disclaimer limits an indemnity.

No deviation to raise, and nothing to trade away here — this section is worth protecting as-is if Vendor proposes changes in later rounds.

Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.

Section 20 meets and exceeds the preferred position. 20.1 gives a Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, with no customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs. 20.2 adds the remaining preferred triggers: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (plus bodily injury/property damage). 20.4 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no adverse settlement without consent). 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate and refund) expressly "in addition to" the defence obligation, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. Direction is correct: the substantive burden falls on Vendor. Liability treatment also favours us: Section 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include a Party's indemnification obligations, IP infringement, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the 21.1 cap entirely — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Section 19.4 and 19.5 further confirm no warranty remedy or disclaimer limits the indemnities. No redline required.

**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, restrictive covenants).**

- **Issue:** Clause 12.4 (§ 12 Customer Responsibilities) is a one-way covenant binding only us: an 18-month post-termination bar on soliciting **or engaging** *any* person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, with no carve-outs.

It also directly contradicts clause 12.3, which confirms we have made no no-hire commitment and may hire persons responding to general recruitment.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 21 of the MSA already delivers our preferred LOL-CAP position, and in one respect exceeds it:

| Playbook requirement | Document | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Mutual cap | § 21.1 "each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual" | ✅ |
| Greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1M | § 21.1 verbatim, using **"paid or payable"** (not just "paid") | ✅ |
| Mutual exclusion of indirect damages | § 21.2 "neither Party is liable for indirect… consequential" | ✅ |
| Uncapped carve-outs | § 21.3 "Excluded Claims" — confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP | ✅ |

Two points worth noting for the deal file:

- **The cap base is real, not illusory.** "Fees" (§ 1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the 12-month multiplier has genuine substance. The exclusion of a one-time implementation charge is mitigated by the USD 1,000,000 floor, which protects us in a low-spend first year.
- **§ 21.2 is better than our model language.** It deems restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, breach notifications and incident response to be *direct* damages. That closes the usual gap where a vendor concedes an uncapped data-breach carve-out but then argues the actual response costs are excluded consequential damages. We should resist any vendor attempt to trade this sentence away in later rounds.

I also confirmed no competing cap is buried elsewhere: searches for "liability" and "exceed" surfaced only the § 18 insurance limits and § 22 audit-cost provision, and §§ 19–20 contain no aggregate-liability or sole-remedy cap — § 20.5's refund remedy is expressly "in addition to" Vendor's defence obligations, so the IP indemnity remains uncapped via § 21.3.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. (1) Cap: § 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual") and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 — the exact basis and floor we require, using the preferred "paid or payable" formulation rather than "paid". (2) Cap base is not illusory: "Fees" (§ 1.5, p0007) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other Order Form amounts, i.e. substantive recurring revenue; the carve-out of a one-time implementation charge does not undermine the base, and the USD 1,000,000 floor protects against a low-fee first year. (3) Indirect damages: § 21.2 excludes consequential/indirect damages mutually ("neither Party"), and helpfully deems data-restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs to be direct damages — better than our position. (4) Carve-outs: "Excluded Claims" (§ 21.3) sits outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion and covers every required item — breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement/misappropriation of the other Party's IP. So the § 20.1 IP indemnity, § 20.2 data-breach indemnity, and §§ 15–17 data/confidentiality/security obligations are all uncapped. (5) § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and is not limited by the section, as we require. No competing or one-sided cap is hidden elsewhere: searches for "liability" and "exceed" return only § 18 insurance limits and § 22 audit-cost language, and §§ 19–20 contain no aggregate-liability or sole-remedy cap (§ 20.5 adds a refund remedy "in addition to" Vendor's defence obligations). § 21.4 is standard savings language. No redline required.

Original paragraphs:

paragraphs.text: 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.
8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.
7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 2.2 (p0013)**

Section 2.2 makes Vendor our "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" — an open-scope exclusivity/field-of-use restriction on us, with no product-level definition, no term cap, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment).

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: delete Section 2.2 in full, with the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, internal-development/acquisition carve-outs) offered in the comment if Vendor needs protection.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 2.2 is an undefined-scope exclusivity/field-of-use restriction binding Customer: it prevents us from sourcing (or arguably building) any hosted analytics services from anyone else for the whole term, with no product-level scope, no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, and no cap. That breaches the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer) and contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment). Preferred remedy is deletion; the fallback (named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) is offered in the comment if Vendor needs protection.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
30. GENERAL

30.1 The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

30.2 Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

30.3 If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

30.4 This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

30.5 No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

30.6 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

30.7 Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.
30.8 The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

paragraphs.text: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
