paragraphs.text: 10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Clause 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits and remote access to our systems, which is the playbook walk-away position. Cost allocation in 22.2 already matches the preferred 5% underpayment threshold and 22.2 bars direct system access, so 22.1 both breaches the rule and conflicts internally. We amended 22.1 to one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where feasible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with no direct or remote system access.

Original paragraphs:
p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
p0094: 22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

Rendered redline:
p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's usage no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours and off-site wherever feasible, through an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement. Neither Vendor nor its auditor shall have direct or remote access to Customer's systems, and Customer may satisfy an audit by providing relevant records and reports.

Comment:
[Playbook] We replaced the unlimited, unannounced audit right and remote system access with our standard position: one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where feasible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality and with no access to our systems. paragraphs.text: 2. AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

2.2 Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

2.3 Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.

paragraphs.text: 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by Customer to Vendor for any delay in providing a "dependency" — an undefined, potentially minor trigger with no aggregate cap, which could exceed the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Our playbook position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; only service credits or LDs flowing to Customer are acceptable, and no such Customer-payable amount appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 contain no termination fee or penalty). The minimal fix is to delete Section 7.6; if a fixed sum is unavoidable, the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 18 (paragraphs p0073–p0074) already contains a Vendor-side insurance covenant that meets or exceeds our preferred position:

| Playbook (preferred) | Section 18.1 |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occurrence, 2M aggregate | ✅ Matches exactly |

| Cyber/privacy USD 5M where processing Customer Data | ✅ **Exceeds** — required unconditionally, not conditioned on Customer Data processing |
| Workers' comp as required by law | ✅ Matches, plus employer's liability USD 1M (extra) |
| Certificates on request | ✅ In 18.2 |

Additional favorable terms beyond our model language:
- Coverage period runs through the term **and one year afterward**, mirroring our model clause.
- Policies must be from reputable insurers and primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 18 already contains a Vendor-side insurance covenant matching or exceeding our preferred position: CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, professional E&O of USD 2M, cyber and privacy liability of USD 5M (required unconditionally, not only where Customer Data is processed), plus workers' compensation as required by law and employer's liability of USD 1M. Coverage runs through the term and for one year afterward, as in our model language. Section 18.2 adds certificates of insurance and evidence of coverage on request, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirms that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. All obligations bind the Vendor and benefit us, so no redline is needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0073: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
p0074: 18.2 Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the Silverline MSA already delivers our preferred warranty position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike services | § 19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |
| Conformance to documentation | § 19.1 and § 19.2 (material conformity) |
| Duration | § 19.2 — 90 days for Deliverables running from delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later**; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** |
| Repair / replace / refund remedy | § 19.4 — re-perform, repair or replace, with termination-and-refund backstop |
| Compliance with laws; no malicious code | § 19.3 — plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protections |
| Disclaimer must not swallow express warranty | § 19.5 — disclaimer limited to implied warranties, mutual, with express carve-out |

Two points worth noting as favorable to us beyond the baseline: the Deliverable warranty clock starts at the *later* of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and the hosted scope is warranted for the entire subscription term rather than a fixed window. The "sole remedy" narrowing the planner flagged as a risk is absent — § 19.4 affirmatively states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, which dovetails with the Excluded Claims carve-outs in § 21.3.

I also confirmed there is no competing disclaimer elsewhere: searches for "AS IS" and "sole remedy" returned no hits, and §§ 3.1 and 6 (acceptance, with correction cycles and refund rights) reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 19 satisfies each element of the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus a material conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables. Section 19.2 provides the 90-day Deliverable conformity period running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later (better than delivery-only), and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop, and expressly states the remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties only, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere in the document, and Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty. No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0076: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
p0078: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.
p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by Customer to Vendor for any delay in providing a "dependency" — an undefined, potentially minor trigger with no aggregate cap, which could exceed the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Our playbook position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; only service credits or LDs flowing to Customer are acceptable, and no such Customer-payable amount appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 contain no termination fee or penalty). The minimal fix is to delete Section 7.6; if a fixed sum is unavoidable, the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") already satisfies the preferred playbook position, and in places improves on it:

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 2.1 correctly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and that a decision not to order is not a breach or shortfall, and Section 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges. However, Section 2.2 imposes a sole-source exclusivity obligation on Customer for hosted analytics for the whole term, which is a restriction on our purchasing volume equivalent to a de facto commitment and has no reduction or exit right. It also contradicts Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. Preferred position is deletion so fees are for ordered or used Services only; deletion is a one-paragraph edit and is proportionate.

Original paragraphs:
p0013: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
p0012: 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
p0050: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies each element of the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus a material conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables. Section 19.2 provides the 90-day Deliverable conformity period running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later (better than delivery-only), and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop, and expressly states the remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties only, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere in the document, and Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty. No redline needed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the Silverline MSA already delivers our preferred warranty position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike services | § 19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |
| Conformance to documentation | § 19.1 and § 19.2 (material conformity) |
| Duration | § 19.2 — 90 days for Deliverables running from delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later**; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** |
| Repair / replace / refund remedy | § 19.4 — re-perform, repair or replace, with termination-and-refund backstop |
| Compliance with laws; no malicious code | § 19.3 — plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protections |
| Disclaimer must not swallow express warranty | § 19.5 — disclaimer limited to implied warranties, mutual, with express carve-out |

Two points worth noting as favorable to us beyond the baseline: the Deliverable warranty clock starts at the *later* of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and the hosted scope is warranted for the entire subscription term rather than a fixed window. The "sole remedy" narrowing the planner flagged as a risk is absent — § 19.4 affirmatively states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, which dovetails with the Excluded Claims carve-outs in § 21.3.

I also confirmed there is no competing disclaimer elsewhere: searches for "AS IS" and "sole remedy" returned no hits, and §§ 3.1 and 6 (acceptance, with correction cycles and refund rights) reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text: This warranty package meets or exceeds our preferred position on every element.

input.quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies each element of the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus a material conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables. Section 19.2 provides the 90-day Deliverable conformity period running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later (better than delivery-only), and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop, and expressly states the remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties only, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere in the document, and Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty. No redline needed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the Silverline MSA already delivers our preferred warranty position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike services | § 19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |
| Conformance to documentation | § 19.1 and § 19.2 (material conformity) |
| Duration | § 19.2 — 90 days for Deliverables running from delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later**; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** |
| Repair / replace / refund remedy | § 19.4 — re-perform, repair or replace, with termination-and-refund backstop |
| Compliance with laws; no malicious code | § 19.3 — plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protections |
| Disclaimer must not swallow express warranty | § 19.5 — disclaimer limited to implied warranties, mutual, with express carve-out |

Two points worth noting as favorable to us beyond the baseline: the Deliverable warranty clock starts at the *later* of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and the hosted scope is warranted for the entire subscription term rather than a fixed window. The "sole remedy" narrowing the planner flagged as a risk is absent — § 19.4 affirmatively states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, which dovetails with the Excluded Claims carve-outs in § 21.3.

I also confirmed there is no competing disclaimer elsewhere: searches for "AS IS" and "sole remedy" returned no hits, and §§ 3.1 and 6 (acceptance, with correction cycles and refund rights) reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale:
WARRANTY PERIOD (addressing the failed deterministic check): Section 19.2 sets the Deliverable conformity period at "ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later." The period is spelled out in words rather than as the numeral "90", which is what caused the "period >= 90 days or expressed in months/years" check to fail; ninety days equals 90 days and therefore meets the preferred 90-day services/Deliverable benchmark exactly. The check failure is a false negative on formatting, not a substantive shortfall. Two features in fact exceed the benchmark: the clock runs from the LATER of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and Hosted Services must conform throughout the entire subscription term, which surpasses the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. I have re-cited the quote to Section 19.2 (rather than the remedy in 19.4) so the period language is on the face of the evidence.

REMAINING ELEMENTS: Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full re-perform/repair/replace remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere; Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

NOTED BUT NOT FLAGGED: the malicious-code warranty in 19.3 is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which is narrower than a flat "no malicious code" and would not reach malware negligently passed through in a third-party component. This is a common market formulation and, given the strong non-exclusive remedy and the security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, it does not change the compliant characterization. Worth raising only if this negotiation reopens Section 19 for other reasons. No redline proposed.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Section 19 of the Silverline MSA already delivers our preferred warranty position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike services | § 19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies each element of the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus a material conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables. Section 19.2 provides the 90-day Deliverable conformity period running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later (better than delivery-only), and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop, and expressly states the remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties only, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere in the document, and Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty. No redline needed.

input.quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies each element of the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus a material conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables. Section 19.2 provides the 90-day Deliverable conformity period running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later (better than delivery-only), and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop, and expressly states the remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties only, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere in the document, and Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty. No redline needed.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the Silverline MSA already delivers our preferred warranty position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike services | § 19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |
| Conformance to documentation | § 19.1 and § 19.2 (material conformity) |
| Duration | § 19.2 — 90 days for Deliverables running from delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later**; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** |
| Repair / replace / refund remedy | § 19.4 — re-perform, repair or replace, with termination-and-refund backstop |
| Compliance with laws; no malicious code | § 19.3 — plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protections |
| Disclaimer must not swallow express warranty | § 19.5 — disclaimer limited to implied warranties, mutual, with express carve-out |

Two points worth noting as favorable to us beyond the baseline: the Deliverable warranty clock starts at the *later* of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and the hosted scope is warranted for the entire subscription term rather than a fixed window. The "sole remedy" narrowing the planner flagged as a risk is absent — § 19.4 affirmatively states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, which dovetails with the Excluded Claims carve-outs in § 21.3.

I also confirmed there is no competing disclaimer elsewhere: searches for "AS IS" and "sole remedy" returned no hits, and §§ 3.1 and 6 (acceptance, with correction cycles and refund rights) reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

input.rationale:
WARRANTY PERIOD (addressing the failed deterministic check): Section 19.2 sets the Deliverable conformity period at "ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later." The period is spelled out in words rather than as the numeral "90", which is what caused the "period >= 90 days or expressed in months/years" check to fail; ninety days equals 90 days and therefore meets the preferred 90-day services/Deliverable benchmark exactly. The check failure is a false negative on formatting, not a substantive shortfall. Two features in fact exceed the benchmark: the clock runs from the LATER of delivery or acceptance rather than delivery alone, and Hosted Services must conform throughout the entire subscription term, which surpasses the 12-month software benchmark for the hosted scope. I have re-cited the quote to Section 19.2 (rather than the remedy in 19.4) so the period language is on the face of the evidence.

REMAINING ELEMENTS: Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications. Section 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and adds no-functionality-diminishment and open-source protections. Section 19.4 supplies the full re-perform/repair/replace remedy with a termination-and-refund backstop and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, and indemnified claims, so the "sole remedy" narrowing we resist is absent. Section 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties, is mutual, and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. No "AS IS" or sole-remedy language appears anywhere; Sections 3.1 and 6 reinforce rather than undercut the warranty.

NOTED BUT NOT FLAGGED: the malicious-code warranty in 19.3 is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which is narrower than a flat "no malicious code" and would not reach malware negligently passed through in a third-party component. This is a common market formulation and, given the strong non-exclusive remedy and the security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, it does not change the compliant characterization. Worth raising only if this negotiation reopens Section 19 for other reasons. No redline proposed.

content.text:
That is the real answer. The document's architecture creates a genuine gap I had missed:

- § 1.7 **Services** = *hosted* software + services → gets full-term conformity under § 19.2.
- § 1.4 **Deliverable** = reports, configurations, integrations, designs → gets ninety days.
- § 13.2 contemplates **software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up/perpetual basis** — non-hosted software, which gets at best the ninety-day Deliverable period, versus our preferred **12 months for software**.

So this is a parametric shortfall, not merely a formatting artifact. Let me validate a minimal fix.

input.summary: Extend the Deliverable conformity period to twelve (12) months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding perpetually/paid-up licensed software or Vendor Technology; keep ninety (90) days for other Deliverables and add numerals.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale:
On re-examination there is a genuine parametric shortfall, not merely the formatting false negative I reported twice before. The preferred position requires twelve months of conformity for SOFTWARE and ninety days for services. The document's definitions split software into two tracks and only one is adequately warranted:

(1) Section 1.7 defines "Services" as the HOSTED software plus implementation and related services. Hosted software is fully covered: Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conformity "throughout the subscription term", which meets or exceeds the twelve-month software benchmark.

(2) Section 13.2, however, expressly contemplates "software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable", granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. That software is not hosted, so the full-term Hosted Services warranty does not reach it. Section 1.4 defines "Deliverable" as reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials and expressly EXCLUDES Vendor Technology. So perpetually licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — the fallback level, not the preferred twelve months. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably carries no durational conformity period at all.

REDLINE: a single minimal amendment to Section 19.2 extends the period to twelve (12) months for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed on a paid-up or perpetual basis, leaving ninety days for all other (services-type) Deliverables. This also renders the period in numerals, which resolves the deterministic period check that failed on the spelled-out "ninety days". Fallback: ninety days across the board if Vendor confirms software is always delivered hosted.

ALL OTHER ELEMENTS REMAIN COMPLIANT and are untouched: 19.1 professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 19.3 malicious code and Applicable Law; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace with termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed. The ninety-day clock also runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is better than the delivery-only benchmark. Separately noted: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", narrower than a flat no-malicious-code warranty; left unflagged as standard market language given the non-exclusive remedy and security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under 21.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services for the full subscription term, but software and Vendor Technology licensed to us on a paid-up or perpetual basis under Section 13.2 is not hosted and so receives only the ninety-day Deliverable period. Our position is twelve months of conformity for software, so we have extended the period for software Deliverables while leaving ninety days for all other Deliverables; we can accept ninety days across the board as a fallback if the software is in practice always delivered hosted.

payload.rationale:
On re-examination there is a genuine parametric shortfall, not merely the formatting false negative I reported twice before. The preferred position requires twelve months of conformity for SOFTWARE and ninety days for services. The document's definitions split software into two tracks and only one is adequately warranted:

(1) Section 1.7 defines "Services" as the HOSTED software plus implementation and related services. Hosted software is fully covered: Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conformity "throughout the subscription term", which meets or exceeds the twelve-month software benchmark.

(2) Section 13.2, however, expressly contemplates "software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable", granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. That software is not hosted, so the full-term Hosted Services warranty does not reach it. Section 1.4 defines "Deliverable" as reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials and expressly EXCLUDES Vendor Technology. So perpetually licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — the fallback level, not the preferred twelve months. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably carries no durational conformity period at all.

REDLINE: a single minimal amendment to Section 19.2 extends the period to twelve (12) months for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed on a paid-up or perpetual basis, leaving ninety days for all other (services-type) Deliverables. This also renders the period in numerals, which resolves the deterministic period check that failed on the spelled-out "ninety days". Fallback: ninety days across the board if Vendor confirms software is always delivered hosted.

ALL OTHER ELEMENTS REMAIN COMPLIANT and are untouched: 19.1 professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 19.3 malicious code and Applicable Law; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace with termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed. The ninety-day clock also runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is better than the delivery-only benchmark. Separately noted: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", narrower than a flat no-malicious-code warranty; left unflagged as standard market language given the non-exclusive remedy and security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under 21.3.

proposal.summary: Extend the Deliverable conformity period to twelve (12) months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding perpetually/paid-up licensed software or Vendor Technology; keep ninety (90) days for other Deliverables and add numerals.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services for the full subscription term, but software and Vendor Technology licensed to us on a paid-up or perpetual basis under Section 13.2 is not hosted and so receives only the ninety-day Deliverable period. Our position is twelve months of conformity for software, so we have extended the period for software Deliverables while leaving ninety days for all other Deliverables; we can accept ninety days across the board as a fallback if the software is in practice always delivered hosted.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding revised: Deviation** (was compliant) — one minimal edit to § 19.2, validated `ok:true`.

My first two passes were wrong in substance, not just in citation. I had treated the failed period check as purely a formatting artifact and kept resubmitting the same conclusion. Pushing past that assumption surfaced a real gap in the definitional architecture:

- **§ 1.7** defines *Services* as the **hosted** software — fully covered, since § 19.2 warrants Hosted Services "throughout the subscription term," which meets the 12-month software benchmark.
- **§ 13.2** separately contemplates software and Vendor Technology "delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable," under a perpetual licence. This is **not hosted**, so the full-term warranty never reaches it.
- **§ 1.4** defines *Deliverable* as reports, configurations, designs and training materials, and expressly **excludes Vendor Technology**. So perpetually licensed software catches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — our *fallback* level, not preferred. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably gets no durational period at all.

The redline extends the period to twelve (12) months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding paid-up/perpetual software, leaving ninety days for services-type Deliverables. It touches one sentence and renders the period in numerals, which also clears the deterministic check honestly rather than by argument.

Everything else in § 19 stands as compliant and is untouched: the professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties, malicious code and Applicable Law, the non-exclusive repair/replace/refund remedy, and § 19.5's implied-only disclaimer with express warranties preserved.

Two caveats worth your judgment. First, confidence is 0.78 rather than higher because the gap is contingent: if Silverline delivers software only as hosted in practice, the ninety-day period is already adequate and the fallback (ninety days across the board) is the sensible landing spot — the Order Forms will tell you which world you are in. Second, I have now reversed the status after the verifier twice affirmed "compliant," so this reversal rests on the § 13.2 / § 1.4 definitional reading rather than on any new verifier instruction; it is worth a second pair of eyes on whether paid-up software delivery is actually in scope for this deal.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
On re-examination there is a genuine parametric shortfall, not merely the formatting false negative I reported twice before. The preferred position requires twelve months of conformity for SOFTWARE and ninety days for services. The document's definitions split software into two tracks and only one is adequately warranted:

(1) Section 1.7 defines "Services" as the HOSTED software plus implementation and related services. Hosted software is fully covered: Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conformity "throughout the subscription term", which meets or exceeds the twelve-month software benchmark.

(2) Section 13.2, however, expressly contemplates "software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable", granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. That software is not hosted, so the full-term Hosted Services warranty does not reach it. Section 1.4 defines "Deliverable" as reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials and expressly EXCLUDES Vendor Technology. So perpetually licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — the fallback level, not the preferred twelve months. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably carries no durational conformity period at all.

REDLINE: a single minimal amendment to Section 19.2 extends the period to twelve (12) months for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed on a paid-up or perpetual basis, leaving ninety days for all other (services-type) Deliverables. This also renders the period in numerals, which resolves the deterministic period check that failed on the spelled-out "ninety days". Fallback: ninety days across the board if Vendor confirms software is always delivered hosted.

ALL OTHER ELEMENTS REMAIN COMPLIANT and are untouched: 19.1 professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 19.3 malicious code and Applicable Law; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace with termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed. The ninety-day clock also runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is better than the delivery-only benchmark. Separately noted: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", narrower than a flat no-malicious-code warranty; left unflagged as standard market language given the non-exclusive remedy and security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under 21.3.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** Legal (Counsel to Customer)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. On balance, the ri[REDACTED] architecture is strong for us: the core protections — indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law (§ 28) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) — are all compliant, and several exceed our preferred positions (notably the uncapped Excluded Claims in § 21.3 and the perpetual, fully paid licence in § 13.2).

The problems are concentrated in a small number of Vendor-favourable clauses that were bolted onto an otherwise balanced document, and three of them sit at our walk-away thresholds:

- **Exclusivity / non-compete (§ 2.2)** — an unlimited sole-supplier commitment binding us for the full term, which also contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. This single clause drives three separate findings (exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment).
- **Liquidated damages (§ 7.6)** — uncapped USD 25,000 per day payable by *us* for delay in an undefined "dependency".
- **Audit rights (§ 22.1)** — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems, which also conflicts internally with § 22.2.

We also flag a Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2), a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-hire (§ 12.4), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right (§ 9), and a narrow warranty gap for perpetually licensed software (§ 19.2). Redlines have been prepared for each deviation; fallbacks are offered in the margin comments where sensible.

---

## 2. Findings

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 5 | High | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22 Audit Rights | § 22.1 permits unlimited, unannounced audits and remote system access (walk-away); conflicts with § 22.2. Redlined to one audit per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site, independent auditor, no system access. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.2 sole-supplier commitment for hosted analytics for the whole term, no scope, time or performance exit (walk-away); contradicts § 2.1. Deleted. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.6 uncapped USD 25,000/day payable by Customer for delay in an undefined "dependency" (walk-away). Deleted; fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. |

| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County; no arbitration provision. No redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.2 requires Customer to extend Vendor our best terms given to any other technology supplier, unqualified as to product, duration and comparability (walk-away). Deleted. |

| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | § 12.4 is one-way, 18 months, covers any Vendor employee during the term, bars "engage" as well as "solicit", no carve-outs; conflicts with § 12.3. Deleted; mutual 12-month fallback offered. |

Amended § 19.2 to 12 months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding such software; 90 days retained for other Deliverables. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following are at our stated walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity / sole-supplier commitment.** An open-ended, term-length restriction on where we source hosted analytics, with no category limit, time limit or performance-based exit. It is internally inconsistent with § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment). We require deletion; the fallback we can offer is a named competing product, term only, capped at 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day, uncapped, triggered by delay in an undefined "dependency". Exposure could exceed the remaining contract value. Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; if Vendor needs a fixed sum, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** An unqualified obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier. Deletion is required; MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access.** Direct or remote access to our systems is not available, and § 22.2 already contradicts it. We accept the § 22.2 5% underpayment cost-allocation threshold as drafted.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Deletions at §§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6 and 12.4; amendments at §§ 8.2, 19.2 and 22.1; new § 9.4 (Customer termination for convenience, 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund consistent with the existing § 10.2 refund mechanic).
2. **Frame the four walk-away items together** in the cover note so Vendor understands they are not trade-able against the compliant clauses at §§ 13, 14, 20, 21 and 24, which we are not reopening.
3. **Flag the internal inconsistencies** created by § 2.2 (against §§ 2.1 and 12.3) and § 22.1 (against § 22.2), and by § 12.4 (against § 12.3). Deleting the offending provisions resolves each conflict and should be an easy concession for Vendor's drafters. Deleting § 7.2 also resolves the duplicate "7.2" numbering with the invoicing clause.
4. **Confirm one factual point with Vendor** for the § 19.2 warranty: if all software is in fact delivered hosted, we can accept 90 days across the board and withdraw the 12-month amendment.
5. **Hold fallbacks in reserve** for the second round: 60-day non-renewal notice (§ 8.2); mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to involved personnel with standard carve-outs (§ 12.4); scope-limited, time-capped exclusivity (§ 2.2); capped early-termination fee in lieu of § 7.6.
6. **Route to the business** for confirmation that a 30-day convenience right and the removal of exclusivity align with the sourcing roadmap before we send."}

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following are at our stated walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity / sole-supplier commitment.** An open-ended, term-length restriction on where we source hosted analytics, with no category limit, time limit or performance-based exit. It is internally inconsistent with § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment). We require deletion; the fallback we can offer is a named competing product, term only, capped at 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day, uncapped, triggered by delay in an undefined "dependency". Exposure could exceed the remaining contract value. Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; if Vendor needs a fixed sum, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** An unqualified obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier. Deletion is required; MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access.** Direct or remote access to our systems is not available, and § 22.2 already contradicts it. We accept the § 22.2 5% underpayment cost-allocation threshold as drafted.
